subtopics.title: Origins, Ideology and Causes of LWE
subtopics.summary: Left Wing Extremism (LWE) traces back to a 1967 uprising in Naxalbari, West Bengal, and aims at societal and political change through revolutionary methods. Its ideology seeks to overthrow the central government through armed revolution and to set up a communist state based on Maoist principles. The booklet links the movement's growth to tribal displacement, tribal resentment over forest laws, poverty and weak governance.
facts: Originated in the 1967 uprising in Naxalbari, West Bengal
Aim: societal and political change through revolutionary methods
Ideology: overthrow the central government through armed revolution
Methods include violence and guerrilla warfare
Goal: establish a communist state based on Maoist principles
Massive displacement of tribal population due to development projects and mining operations
Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 prohibits tribes from harvesting forest resources
Poverty and lack of sustainable means drive people to join the Naxalite movement
Lack of effective governance is a listed factor responsible for the movement
Insufficient technical intelligence against Naxalism is a listed factor responsible for the movement

subtopics.title: Current LWE Landscape and Factors Behind the Decline
subtopics.summary: The booklet reports a sharp fall in LWE-affected districts, from 126 in 2014 to about 7 in 2026, with the remaining hotspots in Chhattisgarh. Violence fell as well, with incidents down 88% and deaths down 90% between 2010 and 2025. The measures credited for this include tactical operations, road and mobile connectivity, action against funding networks, surrender incentives and administrative expansion.
facts: LWE-affected districts reduced from 126 (2014) to about 7 (2026)
Residual hotspots: Bijapur, Sukma and Narayanpur in Chhattisgarh
Incidents of violence down 88%: 1,936 in 2010 to 234 in 2025
Deaths down 90%: 1,005 in 2010
Red Corridor: severe Naxalism-Maoist insurgency across ten listed states, including Kerala and Telangana
Tactical dominance by COBRA and Greyhounds, using company operating bases to penetrate remote zones
Infrastructure integration: 12,000 km of all-weather roads reduced geographical isolation of insurgents
Information warfare: 9,000+ mobile (4G) towers countered Maoist propaganda and integrated tribal regions digitally
Financial crackdown: NIA and Enforcement Directorate action and asset seizures disrupted urban funding networks
Surrender-cum-Rehabilitation Policy: 10,000+ cadres surrendered since 2014, with cash benefits and skill training

subtopics.title: Government Initiatives: Policy, SAMADHAN and Tribal Development
subtopics.summary: The government's response combines a 2015 national policy and action plan with the SAMADHAN doctrine, a set of eight elements running from leadership to financing. Parallel development schemes target tribal regions, including the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan and PM-JANMAN. The booklet also cites the 2006 Bandyopadhyay Committee, which highlighted governance and discrimination gaps faced by tribals.
facts: National Policy and Action Plan to address Left Wing Extremism, 2015
SAMADHAN doctrine: Smart leadership, Aggressive strategy, Motivation and training, Actionable intelligence
SAMADHAN also covers Dashboard based KPIs and KRAs, Harnessing technology, Action plan for each theatre and No access to financing
Special Central Assistance (SCA) supports public infrastructure and services
Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan covers 63,000+ tribal villages, with focus on housing and water
PM-JANMAN targets 75 PVTGs for basic infrastructure and healthcare in remote habitations
Van Dhan Vikas Kendra: 2,200+ clusters promote minor forest produce value addition
Bastariya Battalion: local recruits in Chhattisgarh who know the language and terrain
Bandyopadhyay Committee (2006) highlighted lack of governance and socio-political and cultural discrimination against tribals
Bandyopadhyay Committee recommended tribal-friendly land acquisition and rehabilitation

quizzes.title: Origins and Causes Check
quizzes.passage: Left Wing Extremism, commonly known as Naxalism, is a movement that seeks social and political change through revolutionary methods. Its followers aim to overthrow the central government through armed revolution, relying on violence and guerrilla warfare. Their long-term goal is to establish a communist state based on Maoist principles. The movement has been most active in the forested and tribal parts of central and eastern India, where the state's presence has often been thin. The movement's support has deep roots in the lives of tribal communities. Large numbers of tribal people have been displaced as development projects and mining operations expanded into their homelands. Many tribal families also resent laws that limit their access to forest resources, which are central to their livelihoods. Poverty and a lack of sustainable means of earning a living push many people towards the movement, and a lack of effective governance is also identified as a contributing factor. Any government response therefore has to address the economic and administrative gaps that the movement draws on, alongside security operations. The booklet presents these problems as connected, so a response has to work on several fronts at once. Development work in tribal areas, including basic housing, water and services, is part of this wider approach.

questions.explanation: The booklet says the movement began with the 1967 uprising in Naxalbari, West Bengal.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Left Wing Extremism:
I. Its ideology seeks to establish a communist state based on Maoist principles.
II. It originated from a 1967 uprising in Naxalbari, Bihar.
III. The Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 allows tribes to harvest forest resources.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the uprising was in Naxalbari, West Bengal, and statement III is wrong because the Act prohibits such harvesting.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about government initiatives against LWE:
I. Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan covers more than 63,000 tribal villages.
II. PM-JANMAN targets 175 PVTGs.
III. Van Dhan Vikas Kendra has more than 2,200 clusters promoting minor forest produce value addition.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II is wrong because PM-JANMAN targets 75 PVTGs.

questions.q: Which state is the Greyhounds, an elite commando force, associated with?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Greyhounds as an elite commando force in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q: Which ministry officially declared India Naxal-Free?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Ministry of Home Affairs declared India Naxal-Free.

quizzes.title: Decline and Response Check
quizzes.passage: In recent years, the number of districts affected by Left Wing Extremism has fallen sharply, and violence has declined in step. Security forces have moved into areas that were once hard to reach. Specialised units operating from bases closer to remote zones have pressed the movement hard, while the state has also tried to close the gap between remote regions and the rest of the country. Connectivity has played a major role. Better road links have reduced the geographical isolation in which insurgents once moved, and expanded mobile networks have helped counter propaganda and bring tribal regions into the digital world. The state has also gone after the money that sustains the movement. Investigation agencies have carried out operations and seized assets, which has disrupted the networks that supply funds from urban areas. The movement also depended on its own system of control in some villages. Administrative efforts have aimed to replace that system with state institutions, including residential schools and programmes for aspirational districts. Coordination between states has been another factor, making it harder for armed cadres to escape across state borders. A surrender and rehabilitation policy has encouraged many members to give up violence and take up a new life, with cash benefits and skill training on offer. These steps are described as connected, so success depends on them working together.

questions.q: What figure, as stated in the booklet, is given for mobile (4G) towers deployed under information warfare? (give the number)
questions.explanation: The booklet records deployment of 9,000+ mobile (4G) towers under information warfare.

questions.q: Apart from COBRA, which elite force is named for tactical dominance against Naxals?
questions.explanation: The booklet names COBRA and Greyhounds as the elite forces used for tactical dominance.

questions.q: What is the name of the Maoist parallel governance system that administrative expansion replaced?
questions.explanation: The booklet says administrative expansion replaced Maoist parallel governance, called Janatana Sarkar.

questions.q: How many cadres have surrendered since 2014 under the Surrender-cum-Rehabilitation Policy? (give the number)
questions.explanation: The booklet records 10,000+ cadres surrendered since 2014 under this policy.

questions.q: In which state are the residual hotspots Bijapur, Sukma and Narayanpur located?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists these three districts as the most affected residual hotspots, all in Chhattisgarh.
